answer_1.quote: We present German4All, the first aligned multi-level paraphrasing dataset in German... The dataset supports a range of tasks, including simplification, complexification, and readability-controlled paraphrasing.
answer_1.outputs: Paraphrases of source texts at five distinct readability/complexity levels

answer_2.quote: We evaluated the outputs in terms of the reference-based metrics BLEU, SARI, and BERTscore, as well as with the linguistic annotations FRE, compression rate, number of sentence splits, and number of exact copies.

answer_3.quote: We employ an LLM-as-a-judge... selected gemma-3-27B-it as the judge model... The prompt reuses the questions and evaluation criteria from the human evaluation.
methods: pairwise evaluation of original‑paraphrase pairs via structured JSON prompt

answer_4.quote: In total, 16 native German speakers participated in our human evaluation... For each text pair, we asked the following questions with the answer options in parentheses.
answer_4.guideline: Participants answered a questionnaire (Q1‑Q5) assessing content preservation, information loss/addition, and suitability of the complexity level.
